Findings from National University Broaden Understanding of Sustainability Research (Export Competitiveness of Peruvian Andean Grains: Structural Dynamics and Emerging Water-sustainability Considerations, 2015-2024)

2026 NOV 18-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Ecology Daily News-- Researchers detail new data in Sustainability Research. According to news reporting originating from Trujillo, Peru, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated," Quinoa, kiwicha and ca& ntilde; ihua are strategic Andean grains for Peru, yet whether Peru' s revealed comparative advantage in... 2026 NOV 18 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Ecology Daily News -- Researchers detail new data in Sustainability Research. According to news reporting originating from Trujillo, Peru, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated, "Quinoa, kiwicha and ca & ntilde;ihua are strategic Andean grains for Peru, yet whether Peru's revealed comparative advantage in them has translated into export performance remains poorly documented. Using official MINCETUR/SUNAT and International Trade Centre data for 2015-2024 (ten annual observations), this study applies a deliberately descriptive, historical design based on compound annual growth rates (CAGR), historically delimited sub-periods, volatility measures, unit values and the revealed comparative advantage indices RCA and ARCA."

Our news editors obtained a quote from the research from National University, "Quinoa export volume grew at a CAGR of 2.96%, but growth slowed from 12.0% per year in 2015-2017 to 0.5% per year in 2017-2024, while its unit value fell by 28.3% and its export value remained below the 2015 level. Kiwicha and ca & ntilde;ihua showed rising RCA (+40.2% and +70.0%) but very volatile exports (standard deviation of annual growth of 52.3 and 39.5 percentage points) and falling unit values. In all three grains, stable or rising revealed specialisation coexisted with declining export value, a pattern consistent with a 'comparative advantage trap'. Single-site evidence from Puno on the blue water footprint is treated as exploratory."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "Comparative advantage alone has not secured export competitiveness; differentiation, market diversification and better data are needed."

For more information on this research see: Export Competitiveness of Peruvian Andean Grains: Structural Dynamics and Emerging Water-sustainability Considerations, 2015-2024. Sustainability , 2026;18(20). Sustainability can be contacted at: Mdpi, Mdpi Ag, Grosspeteranlage 5, Ch-4052 Basel, Switzerland.

The news editors report that additional information may be obtained by contacting Heyner Yuliano Marquez Yauri, National University Trujillo, Fac Econ Sci, Profess Sch Adm, Dept. of Administration, Trujillo 13001, Peru. Additional authors for this research include Sandra Lizzette Leon Luyo, Carlos Enrique Cruzado Paredes, Maria Patricia Rodriguez Kong, Catalina Alcira Ramos Laiza, Sergio Antonio Samanamud Pinedo, Manuel Edward Cosme Urbina, Denis Guizela Chavez Bejarano, Jose Alfredo Castaneda Nassi and Aurelio Maximino Carranza Rodriguez.

The direct object identifier (DOI) for that additional information is: https://doi.org/10.3390/su182010676 . This DOI is a link to an online electronic document that is either free or for purchase, and can be your direct source for a journal article and its citation.

The conflict between Cerro Matoso and Canacol Energy over natural gas supply has put the mining company's operations in jeopardy, as it has seen contracted deliveries from the producer progressively decline to nearly zero.

According to figures provided by the company, supply dropped from 16 million cubic feet per day to 11 million in February 226 and subsequently to seven million. By November, deliveries fell to about 3 cubic feet per day, a reduction that forced Cerro Matoso to halt one of its production lines and seek alternatives to ensure continuity of its operations.

This conflict is compounded by the natural gas supply crisis that Colombia is currently facing, amidst the lowest exploratory activity in recent years and the previous government's energy policy decisions led by Gustavo Petro, which did not promote new hydrocarbon exploration contracts.

This situation has increased reliance on the external market: at present, imported gas accounts for 44% of the national supply. In this context, Cerro Matoso's president, Ricardo Gaviria Jansa, explained the difficulties in the industry in an interview with Portafolio.

What is the current situation with Canacol?

Canacol cut us off completely. We had to stop one production line. We ended up at zero because we no longer had the excess gas that Hocol provided.

With the help of the government and other companies, we have managed to secure gas. But I believe the time has come for us to take action.

What do you expect from the Superintendency of Companies' decision regarding the ruling from Canada?

I believe it will be in favor of the industry. Now, whether it comes out in the way we hope—meaning we don't want the 1% that the Canadian Court indicates—I don't think that's going to happen.

The Canadian Court itself stated that if Cerro Matoso's contracts were canceled, there would be a complex public order problem, and that it would have a huge social impact due to the number of people relying on us.

What happens if the Superintendency rules in favor of Cerro Matoso?

I believe that if the Superintendency issues a ruling as we hope and believe it should be, they will have no choice but to stop playing the games they have been playing since this process began.

So, what happens? The search for potential buyers in Canada would have little appetite because they need to proceed with the contracts they currently have.

What they wanted were new contracts with entirely different pricing.

So, in that sense, the National Hydrocarbons Agency will need to define and appoint an operator, which I believe could easily be Hocol or another entity.

What we don't want is for the Canacol well matter to end, as they are currently only producing around 4 to 45 MBTU per day, which is five million cubic feet.

What message are you sending to De La Espriella's Government?

I will tell you one thing; as I have said to everyone: I feel fortunate to meet with government officials at all levels, in all offices, who look at you, listen to you, and discuss matters with you. They say, "This is our position; we are working in a coordinated manner."

However, what happens is that we as an industry would like everything to move faster.

The gas issue has seen four years of neglect.

Before Petro, around 13 gas wells were drilled annually. Under the previous government, only three were drilled on average.

So, there has been a tremendous lack of action.

Today, 4% of the gas is imported.

The latest report states that 44% of the gas used is imported

Every day that passes, the percentage increases by two points, as it was 38% two weeks ago.

Therefore, I believe the message is for continued support, to keep supporting the industry, and to unblock projects.

Because today you cannot impose so much bureaucracy; we need to expedite licenses and permits because drilling is required, and these regasification plants need to start operating as quickly as possible.

Another message is that we need to find ways to prevent abuses in the pricing of the new molecules that will leave the country, as we must not expect that they will be priced at the same value as the imported gas.

This includes Ecopetrol, as it is the largest gas producer in the country.

How much has Cerro Matoso's production fallen, and what has happened with its export markets?

We were supposed to produce 321 tons this year. We will produce 263.

But anticipating all this, we slowed down our sales pace.

So, at this moment, we haven't let anyone down. It would have been worse to breach a contract, which obviously leads to penalties, and clients would not want to see you again.

But we have managed this well with our sales team in Europe and Asia.

What needs to be done now?

The government is doing everything possible to increase drilling.

The Cartagena regasifier, Puerto Bahía, is supposed to be ready by next year, around February or March.

There is another regasifier expected to come online in 2028, which is the Palermo regasifier, in front of the port of Barranquilla. This regasifier is smaller.

Today they are finishing, I believe, finalizing the financial aspects in New York, and construction should begin soon, so it should be ready by 2028.

Additionally, there are some wells and fields in testing. This could generate some interesting gas production.

So, in that sense, the National Hydrocarbons Agency will need to define and appoint an operator, which I believe could easily be Hocol or another entity.

What we don't want is for the Canacol well matter to end, as they are currently only producing around 4 to 45 MBTU per day, which is five million cubic feet.

What message are you sending to De La Espriella's Government?

I will tell you one thing; as I have said to everyone: I feel fortunate to meet with government officials at all levels, in all offices, who look at you, listen to you, and discuss matters with you. They say, "This is our position; we are working in a coordinated manner."

However, what happens is that we as an industry would like everything to move faster.

The gas issue has seen four years of neglect.

Before Petro, around 13 gas wells were drilled annually. Under the previous government, only three were drilled on average.

So, there has been a tremendous lack of action.

Today, 4% of the gas is imported.

The latest report states that 44% of the gas used is imported

Every day that passes, the percentage increases by two points, as it was 38% two weeks ago.

Therefore, I believe the message is for continued support, to keep supporting the industry, and to unblock projects.

Because today you cannot impose so much bureaucracy; we need to expedite licenses and permits because drilling is required, and these regasification plants need to start operating as quickly as possible.

Another message is that we need to find ways to prevent abuses in the pricing of the new molecules that will leave the country, as we must not expect that they will be priced at the same value as the imported gas.

This includes Ecopetrol, as it is the largest gas producer in the country.

How much has Cerro Matoso's production fallen, and what has happened with its export markets?

We were supposed to produce 321 tons this year. We will produce 263.

But anticipating all this, we slowed down our sales pace.

So, at this moment, we haven't let anyone down. It would have been worse to breach a contract, which obviously leads to penalties, and clients would not want to see you again.

But we have managed this well with our sales team in Europe and Asia.

What needs to be done now?

The government is doing everything possible to increase drilling.

The Cartagena regasifier, Puerto Bahía, is supposed to be ready by next year, around February or March.

There is another regasifier expected to come online in 2028, which is the Palermo regasifier, in front of the port of Barranquilla. This regasifier is smaller.

Today they are finishing, I believe, finalizing the financial aspects in New York, and construction should begin soon, so it should be ready by 2028.

Additionally, there are some wells and fields in testing. This could generate some interesting gas production.

Industrias Peñoles, the world's leading silver producer, has signed a 20-year renewable energy supply contract with Atlas Renewable Energy, a U.S. company that develops, builds, and operates energy projects in Latin America.

The contract includes the development of a solar generation and storage project located in the state of Coahuila, which is set to commence operations in the first half of 2029. It will feature a peak solar capacity of 269 megawatts and a battery storage system that will collectively supply around 550 gigawatt hours annually.

"The supply will support part of the electricity demand for its operations in the northern part of the country and is part of the company's strategy to enhance the energy competitiveness of its processes and increase the use of renewable sources," Atlas Renewable Energy stated in a press release.

With this agreement, Atlas Renewable Energy will establish its first renewable energy supply contract with a private client in Mexico, thus expanding its client portfolio, which includes leading companies in the mining, metallurgy, chemical, cement, and technology sectors.

"This contract demonstrates that solar energy with storage is a competitive option for large industries in the country, a technology in which Atlas is a leader in Latin America," said Camilo Serrano, the country manager for Mexico at Atlas Renewable Energy, in the same release. "We thank Peñoles for their trust in our development and implementation capabilities, and we look forward to supporting their growth and that of the mining industry in the country."

Since Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) victory on October 25, the U.S. dollar has increased by 14.8%, and the Brazilian real has recorded the worst performance among the 116 currencies monitored by Austin Rating. This represents the worst currency reaction in the world during this period. The effects of the devaluation are already evident in wholesale markets, where prices have seen the greatest increase in over a year.

According to Jacqueline Neo, head of operations and currency at be.Smart, the devaluation of the real reflects a growing perception of economic risk concerning Brazil.

"The market is attentive to the conduct of fiscal policy, particularly the government's ability to balance revenues and expenditures and to present a sustainable trajectory for public debt," she states.

Fiscal risk pressures inflation expectations

Even with low inflation in October, expectations point to a price acceleration in the coming years. The IPCA (Broad Consumer Price Index) stood at 0.14%, half of the midpoint of financial market projections, according to the Central Bank's Focus Bulletin released a week earlier.

However, inflation expectations for 2027 have risen since the second round of the election. A survey by the Central Bank (BC) with financial institutions indicates that the median projections for the IPCA increased from 4.34% on October 23, before the runoff, to 5% on the last Friday (13).

Stronger dollar increases production costs and reaches store shelves

The devaluation of the real raises production costs for companies that rely on imported inputs and raw materials priced in dollars. As these costs are present at various stages of the production chain, price increases can reach final prices even when the product is made in Brazil.

"The dollar serves as a price reference for a significant portion of the economy. Even products manufactured in Brazil can have costs tied to the U.S. currency, whether due to raw materials, inputs used in production, or transportation. Therefore, a persistent appreciation of the exchange rate can pressure the cost of living for the entire population, regardless of whether individuals have direct dealings with foreign currency," explains Fábio Martini, consultant at Mhydas Financial Planning.

Wholesale prices reach the highest level in over a year

The pressure is already visible in wholesale price indicators. For the 12-month period leading up to November, the Broad Producer Price Index (IPA-10) rose by 5.85%, the highest increase in more than a year, according to the Brazilian Institute of Economics of Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV Ibre).

The indicator has recorded increases for three consecutive months, driven by gasoline, products from the soybean chain, and cattle. The accumulated change over 12 months rose from 2.57% in September to 5.03% in October, reaching 5.85% in November.

The Producer Price Index (IPP), calculated by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), also indicates pressure on industrial costs, albeit with a two-month lag. In September, the latest available data, the indicator recorded an increase of 4.34% compared to the same month in 2025.

The currency devaluation may amplify this pressure in the coming months. "With a stronger dollar, imported inputs may further pressure prices, adding between 0.4 to 0.7 percentage points to the IPCA for 2027. Retail and distribution companies, which are facing consumers more sensitive to price adjustments, may see a compression of margins by 1.5 to 3 percentage points," estimates Letícia Moschioni, partner at Finscale.

Fuel, food, and electronics also feel the pressure

Fuels are among the first products to feel the effects of the exchange rate. Since oil is priced in dollars, the devaluation of the real increases the prices of gasoline and diesel, even when there is no change in the international price of crude oil.

To this effect are added tensions in the Middle East, which are pushing oil and its derivative prices higher. The impact extends beyond gas stations: the road transport of goods also becomes more expensive, spreading costs throughout the logistics chain.

In food, imported wheat influences the prices of products such as bread, pasta, and cookies. Meanwhile, chicken and pork production relies on feed made from corn and soybeans, which are also priced in dollars. Fresh produce, for their part, respond to other factors such as El Niño and seasonality, according to economists from XP Investimentos in a report.

The pressure also reaches electronics and appliances, which use imported components. El Niño reduces the draft of the Amazon rivers—the depth available for navigation—and increases shipping costs for production from the Free Trade Zone of Manaus, one of Brazil's main industrial hubs.

With difficulties in transporting goods via waterways, some cargo must resort to air transport, which has also become more expensive. Aviation kerosene (QAV) sold to distributors has increased by 83.7% in the year, reaching R$ 6.69 per liter. This marks the highest price in 2026, according to Petrobras's monthly adjustments.

The increase reflects the international hike in fuel prices, exacerbated by reduced refining capacity in Russia and Ukraine. The diversion of cargo to air transport occurs precisely at a time of high costs, increasing pressure on electronic prices.

Medications follow a different dynamic. The currency fluctuation is passed on to prices more slowly due to sector regulation and annual adjustment cycles.

Dollar pass-through varies by product

The time it takes for the dollar's rise to reach consumers varies by product. Gasoline and diesel may feel the effects within a few weeks. In contrast, processed and industrialized food depends on stock levels and supply contracts, which can delay the pass-through for months.

According to Martini, it is not the price recorded on a single day that determines the impact on consumers' wallets, but rather the duration for which the dollar remains at a high level. It is this possibility of persistent devaluation that the market has begun to price in more intensely.

The general minimum wage in Mexico could see a significant increase by 2027 , rising from the current 9,582.47 pesos per month to approximately 10,700 pesos .

This projection, supported by the Mexican Institute of Public Accountants (IMCP) , anticipates an adjustment of between 12% and 13% , which would translate into an additional 1,118 pesos per month for workers earning the base salary.

The discussion around the minimum wage increase is gaining national significance, as it directly affects the purchasing power of millions of Mexicans and the economy of businesses.

The annual adjustment is determined by the National Commission of Minimum Wages (Conasami) , which includes representatives from labor, employer, and government sectors.

For 2027, the expectation is that the increase will surpass the inflation rate and maintain the trend of wage recovery observed in recent years.

According to estimates from the IMCP and statements from labor authorities, the new daily minimum could be set between 352 and 355 pesos, consolidating progress towards the six-year goal of ensuring that the minimum wage covers at least 2.5 times the value of the basic basket by 2030.

How is the minimum wage increase defined in Mexico?

The process to determine the minimum wage begins each year with the permanent session of Conasami , which in 2026 will commence negotiations starting on November 26 .

During this time, the labor , employer , and government sectors present their proposals and arguments, considering factors such as annual inflation , economic growth, and the effects of labor reforms, including the reduction of the weekly working hours.

The Mexican Constitution establishes that the minimum wage cannot be increased below the inflation rate, ensuring a real adjustment in workers' income. However, in recent years, wage policy has sought to exceed this legal floor, with double-digit increases aimed at recovering the purchasing power lost in previous decades.

The official resolution regarding the new minimum wage must be published no later than December 1 of each year , to take effect on January 1 of the following year.

What are the proposals from the sectors for 2027?

In the negotiation for the 2027 minimum wage , there are notable differences among the involved sectors:

  • The business sector , represented by organizations like Coparmex , has suggested an increase of between 9% and 9.9% , arguing for the need to maintain competitiveness and avoid excessive inflationary pressures.
  • Trade union organizations , such as CTM and the Congress of Labor , have proposed increases of between 12% and 18% , aiming to accelerate wage recovery and improve workers' living conditions.
  • Conasami , through its president Luis Felipe Munguía Corella, has indicated that the range for discussion is between 10% and 15% , ruling out adjustments lower than double digits.

The IMCP supports the position of an increase of between 12% and 13% , which would set the minimum wage at 10,700 pesos per month in 2027.

What factors influence the adjustment of the minimum wage?

The analysis to define the minimum wage increase considers several key elements:

  • Annual inflation: The increase cannot be less than the recorded inflation rate.
  • Economic growth: The capacity of businesses to absorb the increase without affecting formal employment is evaluated.
  • Reduction of working hours: The potential reduction from 48 to 46 hours per week may elevate operational costs, which is taken into account during negotiations.
  • Purchasing power goal: The federal government aims for the minimum wage to cover 2.5 times the value of the basic basket by 2030.

Furthermore, the wage recovery policy implemented since 2018 has been recognized by national and international organizations, as it has allowed more than 6.6 million people to escape multidimensional poverty, according to studies conducted by Conasami.

What would the minimum wage in the Free Trade Zone of the Northern Border look like?

In the Free Trade Zone of the Northern Border , the minimum wage is higher than in the rest of the country. For 2026, it is set at 440.87 pesos daily (13,409.80 pesos monthly). Although there is no official projection for 2027 yet, it is expected that the percentage increase will be similar to that of the general minimum wage, maintaining the gap between both regions.

What impact would the increase have on workers and the economy?

A minimum wage increase of this magnitude would have direct effects on the income of formal workers earning the base amount, as well as those whose salaries are indexed to the minimum. It could also influence the wage negotiation dynamics in other sectors and the pricing structure of goods and services.

On the other hand, the business sector warns about the risk that higher increments could be passed on to prices, affecting inflation, though recent evidence shows that the increases in previous years have not led to a disproportionate inflationary impact.

When will the minimum wage for 2027 be defined?

The Conasami will initiate formal negotiations in the last week of November 2026 and must publish the official resolution no later than December 1, 2026 . The new minimum wage will come into effect on January 1, 2027 .

Finance Minister Dario Durigan denied on Wednesday (November 18) that the government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) is working to change the inflation target. According to him, the Brazilian economic environment provides security to attract investments.

Follow the Correio Braziliense channel on WhatsApp and receive the day's top news on your mobile.

"We are not discussing any change to Brazil's inflation target. We have built strong capital markets. We have the right conditions to attract capital and show the world that Brazil is the right place to invest, with commitments to the environment, social commitments, and commitments to democracy," said the head of the economic team during a virtual presentation at the 16th Edition of the Bradesco BBI CEO Forum.

Stay updated on the news that matters to you!

This statement comes amid speculation from government officials that the Executive is planning to raise the target set by the National Monetary Council (CMN) as a strategy for the Central Bank to lower the basic interest rate (Selic), which is currently at 13.75% per year.

While acknowledging speculation regarding changes to the inflation target, Durigan stated that he does not see this debate gaining traction within the PT. "There is no risk of this gaining momentum and becoming a majority position in the party," the minister assured, also denying that President Lula's party had taken a definitive stance on any measures for capital control.

Commitments and Reforms

At the event, Durigan also remarked that the fiscal adjustment of the complementary bill (PLP) currently under discussion in the Senate is not ideal and that fiscal risk is the key factor affecting interest rates. He also noted that fiscal action would be the government's main asset in addressing the Selic.

"The fiscal results, the primary results, which the government can control, have improved over the years. Of course, they are not ideal, and we are not meeting all the expectations that the market imposes on us. Fiscal risk is a fundamental aspect in explaining interest rates, but there are other factors at play," the minister explained.

When citing the government's fiscal projection and the outlook for reducing the Selic, Dario Durigan acknowledged market expectations that Brazil will experience lower growth in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) next year. However, he asserted that this slowdown in growth will not lead to a recession.

Durigan's participation in the Bradesco event came right after a meeting between him and Lula. Their conversation at the Palácio da Alvorada revolved around market expectations regarding who will head the Finance Ministry in Lula's fourth term and the political negotiations for the approval of the fiscal adjustment package in the Senate.

Considered a priority for the government, the proposal outlines mechanisms to limit fiscal spending. Initially expected to be approved by the House yesterday (17), the text faced resistance from opposition lawmakers. However, there are expectations from both the government and Senator Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), the rapporteur of the matter, to complete the vote today so that, if approved, it can be sent to the Chamber of Deputies.

By Francisco Artur de Lima

NYSE END-OF-DAY STOCK REPORT

PHOENIX, Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026 - Southern Copper Corporation's (NYSE:SCCO $144.24) stock price traded at its 320-day low of $141.41. The last time the price hit that low level was on Friday, Jan 02, 2026.

Southern Copper Corporation's stock price plunged $11.19 (7.2%) from its previous trading session to close at $144.24.

Compared with the S&P 500 Index which fell 18.1 points (0.2%) in the day, the relative price change was -6.9%.

There were 768,418 shares worth $110.8 million traded today; the volume was 0.6 times the average daily trading volume of 1.2 million shares.

INDEX

SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

SECTION 2 THE PAST YEAR: PRESS RELEASES

STOCK IDENTIFIERS

GLOSSARY

SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. Aug 04, 2026: Fresnillo: Interim Results for the six months to 30 June 2026

Fresnillo plc interim results

for the six months to 30 June 2026

Octavio Alvidrez, Chief Executive Officer, commented:

"Fresnillo delivered an exceptional financial performance in the first half of 2026. Through a combination of solid operational execution and cost discipline, we continued to capitalise on the historic strength of precious metals prices, with revenues up 74.7% to US$3.4 billion, driving Gross Profit up 130.7% to US$2.4 billion and strong operating cash flow. Our financial position enabled us to fund the strategic acquisition of Probe Gold, ongoing capex requirements, investment in exploration, and to declare an increased interim dividend of 43.4 cents per share for the period, in accordance with our dividend policy, while maintaining a robust balance sheet.

"Operationally, gold and silver production was in line with our expectations and plans across our mines are progressing well. We saw year-on-year changes from lower grades, a minor delay in the commissioning of the leaching pad XV at Herradura, and weather-related disruptions.

"We remain focused on managing costs within our control by driving efficiencies across our supply chain and advancing key infrastructure projects, including the interconnection of the Jarillas shaft at Saucito.

"Our full-year production guidance remains unchanged, and our high-margin portfolio puts us in a strong position to capitalise on ongoing market tailwinds. The safety and well-being of our people and host communities remain our core priority as we deliver on our strategy for the remainder of 2026."

Our financial position remains solid, with a net cash position of US$1,916.6 million, enabling us to invest in future growth while maintaining attractive returns to shareholders."

Jan 22, 2026: Fresnillo completes acquisition of Probe Gold

Fresnillo plc Completes Acquisition of Probe Gold Inc.

Fresnillo plc ("Fresnillo" or "the Company") is pleased to announce the successful completion of its acquisition ("Transaction") of Probe Gold Inc. ("Probe") following receipt of all required shareholder, court and regulatory approvals.

Fresnillo has paid approximately CAD$770 million (approx. US$555 million) in settlement of the transaction consideration funded with existing cash on hand.

Transaction Highlights

Entry into Canada - provides immediate access to the prolific Val d'Or district in Quebec, a world-class mining jurisdiction with established infrastructure and a skilled workforce.

Scale and growth - adds a 10 million oz gold resource base, led by the flagship Novador project - an advanced asset capable of producing 200,000+ oz/year for over a decade.

Exploration upside - includes a 1,798 km2 land package with significant growth potential, including the Detour Gold Quebec project, which will leverage Fresnillo's technical expertise.

Strategic alignment - fits Fresnillo's disciplined M&A strategy by acquiring value-driven, early-stage and advance precious metals exploration projects that complement core operations and the existing portfolio.

The Company maintains its strong financial position and there is no change to Fresnillo's dividend policy as a result of this acquisition.

Octavio Alvidrez, Chief Executive Officer of Fresnillo, commented:

"We are delighted to complete the acquisition of Probe. As we announced previously, this acquisition is consistent with our disciplined approach to M&A and meets our strict criteria of having a sizeable resource base with upside optionality in a region with mining history, skilled personnel, and existing infrastructure. We are excited that our first project outside of Mexico is in Canada, an outstanding mining jurisdiction with a global reputation for responsible development, and in the Val d'Or region with its proud history of mining.

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo Mexico, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Chile today faces an economic paradox that is as evident as it is urgent. According to the National Institute of Statistics (INE), the unemployment rate reached 9.8% in the July-September quarter, which translates to over a million people without jobs. However, looking within companies reveals an opposite diagnosis: 62% report difficulties in finding qualified profiles, according to ManpowerGroup, and in the construction sector, 75% of projects report problems hiring workers, according to the Microdata Center of the University of Chile.

The issue in the Chilean labor market is no longer solely about creating jobs but rather about closing the gap between what people know how to do and what industries actually need. On November 17, National Training and Employability Day, the discussion must move beyond good intentions: it requires a rigorous review of how we are training our workforce.

Technological acceleration and new productivity demands are changing trades at a faster pace than our traditional teaching systems can adapt. In labor-intensive sectors—such as construction, mining, or logistics—the lack of qualified technicians and specialists drives up project costs, hampers productivity, and ultimately delays the investments that the country urgently needs. This gap directly threatens the nation's competitiveness in a global context.

To unlock this scenario, a shift in focus is required on two fronts. First, within companies themselves: the development of human capital must move beyond an administrative approach to become integral to strategic planning. Anticipating the competencies that will be required in business over the next two years and retraining current teams is the most profitable investment for maintaining competitiveness today.

Second, in the public-private educational ecosystem: we must stop measuring the success of training by attendance rates or the number of hours delivered. The only metric that matters is whether that training translates into effective employability, job mobility, and increased productivity in the workplace.

Chile needs to reactivate investment to grow again, but projects do not execute themselves. If we do not urgently align workforce training with the real demands of the labor market, and if we do not view training as an investment rather than a public expense, we will continue to have a million people seeking opportunities while industries struggle to take off due to a lack of talent.

By José Esteban Garay, General Manager of OTIC CChC

On the occasion of World Corn Day, Mexico is facing a critical scenario characterized by an increasing dependence on imports and a alarming decrease in harvested acreage. According to estimates from the Agricultural Markets Consulting Group (GCMA), by 2026, national production will reach only 23.5 million tons against an apparent consumption of 48.2 million tons, placing the self-sufficiency index at around 49 percent.

This decline is directly linked to the reduction in cultivated lands, as observed in the spring-summer cycle, where 5.4 million hectares were harvested compared to 6.2 million in previous years, or in Sinaloa, where only 584,000 of the 800,000 available irrigated hectares were planted, resulting in a 17% abandonment of corn acreage between 2018 and 2026.

Experts such as Juan Carlos Anaya (GCMA) and Samuel Sarmiento (UAS) agree that this deterioration is not a temporary issue but rather the outcome of poor public policy decisions compounded by adverse market and climate factors. Producers are navigating through a "storm" marked by low international prices, the appreciation of the peso, droughts, and a significant rise in input costs for fertilizers, seeds, and diesel, which will increase the cost of cultivation to 54,365 pesos per hectare for the upcoming cycle, according to FIRA.

Additionally, there is a lack of access to competitive credit and climate insurance, causing thousands of farmers to fall into default and reduce their investments. While the federal government's intention to implement commercial management schemes and insurance for white corn in 2026 is acknowledged, experts emphasize that current measures are insufficient.

To reverse the crisis, Anaya proposes a long-term national policy based on five fundamental pillars: competitive financing with guarantees, comprehensive management of climate risks, schemes that ensure profitability (such as target income and coverage), boosting productivity through technology and technical assistance, and clear marketing rules before planting begins.

Meanwhile, Sarmiento Gámez warns that achieving food sovereignty requires the creation of a new first-tier development bank that provides direct loans without intermediaries that inflate financing costs, as well as the allocation of multi-year budgets for health, modernization, and marketing.

Both analysts also emphasize the urgency of reinstating contract farming and the purchase of coverage on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, instruments that were eliminated in the previous administration and provided certainty to producers about who would buy their harvest and at what minimum price before planting.

They also criticized the recent governmental strategy for prioritizing assistance programs that, in their view, "only serve to distribute money" without incentivizing productivity. Given that 82% of Mexican farmers cultivate on rain-fed plots of less than five hectares with an average yield of only 2.5 tons per hectare, without structural changes in rural policies, Mexico is not positioned to achieve food security or self-sufficiency in this staple grain.

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Nine years after joining the American Colombian Chamber of Commerce, María Claudia Lacouture has resigned from the presidency of the bilateral business body between Colombia and the United States. She is now preparing to move to the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean.

"With a heart full of gratitude, I submitted my resignation as president of @AmChamCol. It has been 9 years of learning and significant achievements shared. Thank you to the Board, the members, and my team for everything," Lacouture shared on X.

The former Minister of Commerce signed her resignation letter on November 16, directed to Juan Pablo Rivera, president of the Board of Directors. On Wednesday, November 18, the chamber made it public.

The Board accepted her resignation, which will take effect on December 18; in the meantime, the Chamber will initiate a selection process to choose her successor, according to its internal policies.

Continue reading: Newly elected government met with AmCham to review tariffs imposed by Trump

What Lacouture Will Do at CAF

Starting in January 2027, she will lead CAF's tourism agenda, the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, with a focus on Ibero-America, operating from Panama.

It is worth noting that tourism has been a constant throughout her professional career. For example, she presided over ProColombia from 2010 to 2016, the agency that promotes exports, foreign investment, and tourism, and later served as Minister of Commerce, Industry, and Tourism under President Juan Manuel Santos from 2016 to 2017. She also authored a book on sustainable tourism.

"Tourism generates wealth and jobs, connects long-distant territories, and tangibly changes people's lives," she wrote in her farewell letter.

Additionally, CAF is a multilateral bank that lends to governments and finances projects in the region, with Colombia being one of its shareholder countries. Having a Colombian manage the tourism agenda from there places someone knowledgeable about the country in an office capable of directing credit and technical cooperation towards destinations, infrastructure, and employment in the sector.

Nine Years Between Bogotá and Washington

Lacouture joined AmCham in October 2017, shortly after leaving the Ministry of Commerce. At that time, the position was referred to as executive director.

The Board summarizes her tenure by stating that the Chamber "grew in reach, voice, and prestige," becoming a key interlocutor for businesses, governments, and media in both countries. Lacouture herself reflected, "When we started this work in 2017, few would have predicted where we would reach."

The most emphasized point in the statement is the bilateral relationship, as under her leadership, AmCham maintained direct lines of communication with the U.S. Embassy in Bogotá, the State Department, the Department of Commerce, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), and Colombian authorities.

This is significant given that the United States is Colombia's main trading partner, with the free trade agreement between the two countries in effect since 2012. When political relations become strained, exporters of flowers, coffee, fruits, or garments, and the jobs dependent on them are the first to feel the impact.

The Board acknowledges that this work continued "even in demanding times." There were indeed such times. In January 2025, the White House threatened tariffs on Colombian products following tensions over deportation flights, and in September of that year, Washington decertified Colombia's efforts in the anti-drug fight.

There were also frictions with the Colombian government. In a public exchange, then Acting Minister of Commerce, Cielo Rusinque, responded that "the government of Colombia does not have unofficial spokespersons." Lacouture countered that in a relationship between countries, each entity has its responsibilities, and the private sector must help keep trade channels open.

BUENOS AIRES, 18 nov (Reuters) - El riesgo país argentino se ubicaba el jueves en torno al umbral de las 850 unidades, un nivel muy alto que a criterio de analistas podría presionar sobre el refinanciamiento de deuda a corto plazo que debe afrontar el Gobierno.

Ante la imposibilidad de acceder al crédito internacional, Argentina busca cada mes postergar amortizaciones mediante diferentes mecanismos financieros internos.

Así, el martes el Tesoro obtuvo el canje de deuda a corto plazo por 2.875 millones de dólares, equivalente a un 60,19% de la propuesta original. Además, tiene en agenda otra licitación de deuda para antes de fin de mes, un hecho vital para medir la liquidez del mercado.

"Se vienen vencimientos por arriba de los 20.000 millones de dólares en lo que queda del 2026 y todo el 2027, con el condicionante de elecciones presidenciales en el medio, por lo que la refinanciación está en el ojo de los inversores para ver cómo se cubrirán esas obligaciones", dijo el analista Marcelo Rojas.

El riesgo país elaborado por el J.P. Morgan se ubicaba en los 848 puntos básicos a las 2000 GMT, similar al nivel de inicios de noviembre y entre el máximo en comparación a un año atrás.

El presidente libertario Javier Milei no logra hacer crecer a la economía como lo pretendía para ayudar a bajar la pobreza e indigencia, en momentos en que la inflación se mueve en torno al 2% mensual con recorte del poder adquisitivo.

Los argentinos irán a las urnas a fines del año próximo en comicios presidenciales, en los que Milei anunció que buscará la reelección.

La deuda pública extrabursátil finalizó con una merma de 0,1% promedio, tras cotizar en leve alza gran parte de la jornada, y luego de perder un 0,4% promedio a inicio de semana, junto a un tipo de cambio algo más activo y con el seguimiento del banco central (BCRA), entidad que acumula compras por unos 16.250 millones de dólares en el transcurso del año.

La entidad monetaria informó la compra de 11 millones de dólares para sus reservas.

El peso mayorista se depreció un 0,45% a 1.559,5 por dólar ARS=RASL y la moneda argentina en un acotado segmento marginal (blue) retrocedía un 1,53% a 1.630 unidades por dólar, anotando su nivel mínimo históricoARSB=.

"De cara a los próximos meses, consideramos atractivos los (títulos) 'Bontam', dado que vemos poco margen para una baja sostenida de la (tasa) 'Tamar' y esperamos que las tasas reales se mantengan en terreno positivo de cara a las elecciones", comentó Delphos Investment.

"La mayor demanda estacional de pesos, el proceso desinflacionario y la prioridad del Gobierno de mantener la estabilidad cambiaria respaldan esta expectativa", acotó.

En este escenario de prudencia entre ahorristas, el índice accionario MSCI Merval .MMXMRVLGA de la bolsa de Buenos Aires mejoró apenas un 0,16%, apoyado principalmente por firmas del rubro energético.

(Reporte de Jorge Otaola;
colaboración de Hernán Nessi;
Editado por Maximilian Heath y Lucila Sigal)

BOGOTÁ, 18 nov (Reuters) - Colombia logró concretar compromisos de inversión con empresas y financiamiento con la banca multilateral por 43.200 millones de dólares, informó el miércoles el vicepresidente del país, José Manuel Restrepo, en momentos en que la nación sudamericana atraviesa por dificultades fiscales y una desaceleración económica.

Los compromisos, que se ejecutarían durante el periodo del Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella, que finaliza en agosto de 2030, incluyen préstamos por 21.400 millones de dólares previstos por el Banco Mundial, el Banco de Desarrollo de América Latina y el Caribe (CAF) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID), precisó Restrepo en su cuenta de X.

El monto total duplicó la meta prevista por el Gobierno en la denominada Milagro Week, una ronda de reuniones de 3 días con inversionistas y bancos de inversión en Nueva York, que terminó el miércoles, agregó el vicepresidente.

Los compromisos incluyen inversiones de las mineras AngloGold Ashanti y Collective Mining; la modernización y ampliación de cinco aeropuertos del país; la sustitución de cultivos ilícitos por productos agrícolas productivos; la creación de un data center de inteligencia artificial y la apertura de nuevos mercados por parte de una cadena comercial, entre otros, según Restrepo.

Pero algunos empresarios condicionaron sus inversiones a una mejora en la seguridad jurídica y la obtención de licencias para desarrollar los proyectos, unos de los principales escollos en el país andino.

Colombia atraviesa por un fuerte deterioro de sus finanzas públicas y una fase de desaceleración de su economía, que en se expandió un 0,5% anual en el tercer trimestre, muy por debajo de lo esperado por el mercado; en tanto que arrojó una contracción de 0,8% en comparación con el segundo trimestre.

(Reporte de Nelson Bocanegra)

(( Nelson.bocanegra@thomsonreuters.com ; +571-5185380; Reuters Messaging: Nelson.bocanegra.reuters.net@reuters.com ))

Actualiza con cotizaciones por la tarde

Por Manuel Farías

SANTIAGO, 18 nov (Reuters) - Las principales monedas y bolsas de América Latina cayeron el miércoles, presionadas por las expectativas de alzas de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos tras comentarios de tono restrictivos de parte de autoridades del banco central y luego de conocerse las minutas de la última reunión del organismo.

* "Casi todos" los responsables monetarios coincidieron en que serían necesarias más alzas de tasas si la economía evolucionaba según lo previsto, según las minutas, mientras que unos pocos señalaron que la inflación podría resultar más persistente y requerir "un cambio hacia una orientación de política monetaria más restrictiva".

* Las expectativas de incrementos en el costo del crédito por parte de la Fed hacía que el índice dólar USD=, que mide el desempeño del billete verde frente a una canasta de seis monedas pares, alcanzara en la jornada máximos de 19 meses, con un alza del 0,22% por la tarde.

* Además, el gobernador de la Fed Christopher Waller dijo el miércoles que el organismo debe adoptar una postura más agresiva en su respuesta a la inflación, ya sea aprobando un alza de medio punto en la reunión de diciembre o comunicando un ritmo más acelerado de alzas para 2027. La inflación "va por mal camino y se está extendiendo", afirmó Waller a la cadena CNBC.

* Durante esta semana, además, datos de ventas minoristas mayores a lo esperado ante cifras de inflación por sobre las expectativas han llevado a los operadores a valorar completamente un alza de 25 puntos básicos en la reunión de diciembre y una pequeña probabilidad de un incremento de 50 puntos, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME Group.

* De acuerdo a la misma herramienta, los operadores ven alrededor de 75 puntos básicos de incremento en 12 meses desde ahora, al rango de 4,50% a 4,75%.

* El peso mexicano MXN= se hundía por la tarde un 2,4%, a 18,8545 unidades por dólar, luego de tres sesiones de alzas; al tiempo que el índice de la bolsa S&P/BMV IPC .MXX perdió un 1,6%, a 69.259,31 puntos, en su cuarta sesión de retroceso.

* El real brasileño BRL= se debilitó un 1,4825%, a 5,8677 unidades por dólar, mientras que el referencial bursátil Bovespa .BVSP bajaba un 1,25%, a 167.687 puntos. Los mercados locales se encuentran atentos, además, a las perspectivas fiscales de la mayor economía de América Latina.

* El peso chileno CLP=CL, CLP= bajó un 1,5% a 1.006,10/1.006,40 unidades por dólar, a su menor valor desde enero de 2025, en medio también del descenso de alrededor del 5% en los precios del cobre, la mayor exportación del país. Asimismo, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA .MMXIPSAGC, retrocedió un 1,09%, a 10.362,70 puntos.

* Rosanna Costa, jefa del Banco Central chileno, dijo en la víspera que la moneda local se estaba moviendo de acuerdo a los fundamentos del mercado.

* Además, la economía chilena cayó un 1,1% interanual en el tercer trimestre afectada por el desempeño del sector minero, según datos del Banco Central del miércoles. El PIB desestacionalizado, en tanto, retrocedió un 1,8% en el periodo respecto al trimestre previo.

* De acuerdo a cifras del banco, es la mayor caída desestacionalizada desde el segundo trimestre de 2020 cuando cedió 12,5%, en los inicios de la pandemia de COVID.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR cedió un 1,59% a 3.356 por dólar; y el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP .COLCAP perdía hacia el cierre un 1,78% a 2.356 puntos, luego de que el Gobierno anunció el martes que la economía se expandió un 0,5% anual en el tercer trimestre, muy por debajo de lo esperado por el mercado; en tanto que arrojó una contracción de 0,8% en comparación con el segundo trimestre.

* El peso mayorista argentino ARS=RASL descendió un 0,45% a 1.559,5 por dólar, mientras que el índice accionario MSCI Merval .MMXMRVLGA de la bolsa de Buenos Aires ganaba un 0,43% antes del cierre.

* El sol peruano PEN=PDSB se depreció un 0,53% a 3,4320/3,4330 unidades por dólar, mientras que el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú realizó un swap cambiario por 700 millones de soles. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPE retrocedió un 2,94% a 1.353 puntos.

(Reporte de Manuel Farías; Reporte adicional de Froilán Romero en Santiago, Nelson Bocanegra en Bogotá, Noé Torres en Ciudad de México, Hernán Nessi y Jorge Otaola en Buenos Aires; Editado por Javier Leira)

((Mesa de Edición en Español; santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com ))

* Las expectativas de incrementos en el costo del crédito por parte de la Fed hacía que el índice dólar USD=, que mide el desempeño del billete verde frente a una canasta de seis monedas pares, alcanzara en la jornada máximos de 19 meses, con un alza del 0,22% por la tarde.

* Además, el gobernador de la Fed Christopher Waller dijo el miércoles que el organismo debe adoptar una postura más agresiva en su respuesta a la inflación, ya sea aprobando un alza de medio punto en la reunión de diciembre o comunicando un ritmo más acelerado de alzas para 2027. La inflación "va por mal camino y se está extendiendo", afirmó Waller a la cadena CNBC.

* Durante esta semana, además, datos de ventas minoristas mayores a lo esperado ante cifras de inflación por sobre las expectativas han llevado a los operadores a valorar completamente un alza de 25 puntos básicos en la reunión de diciembre y una pequeña probabilidad de un incremento de 50 puntos, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME Group.

* De acuerdo a la misma herramienta, los operadores ven alrededor de 75 puntos básicos de incremento en 12 meses desde ahora, al rango de 4,50% a 4,75%.

* El peso mexicano MXN= se hundía por la tarde un 2,4%, a 18,8545 unidades por dólar, luego de tres sesiones de alzas; al tiempo que el índice de la bolsa S&P/BMV IPC .MXX perdió un 1,6%, a 69.259,31 puntos, en su cuarta sesión de retroceso.

* El real brasileño BRL= se debilitó un 1,4825%, a 5,8677 unidades por dólar, mientras que el referencial bursátil Bovespa .BVSP bajaba un 1,25%, a 167.687 puntos. Los mercados locales se encuentran atentos, además, a las perspectivas fiscales de la mayor economía de América Latina.

* El peso chileno CLP=CL, CLP= bajó un 1,5% a 1.006,10/1.006,40 unidades por dólar, a su menor valor desde enero de 2025, en medio también del descenso de alrededor del 5% en los precios del cobre, la mayor exportación del país. Asimismo, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA .MMXIPSAGC, retrocedió un 1,09%, a 10.362,70 puntos.

* Rosanna Costa, jefa del Banco Central chileno, dijo en la víspera que la moneda local se estaba moviendo de acuerdo a los fundamentos del mercado.

* Además, la economía chilena cayó un 1,1% interanual en el tercer trimestre afectada por el desempeño del sector minero, según datos del Banco Central del miércoles. El PIB desestacionalizado, en tanto, retrocedió un 1,8% en el periodo respecto al trimestre previo.

* De acuerdo a cifras del banco, es la mayor caída desestacionalizada desde el segundo trimestre de 2020 cuando cedió 12,5%, en los inicios de la pandemia de COVID.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR cedió un 1,59% a 3.356 por dólar; y el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP .COLCAP perdía hacia el cierre un 1,78% a 2.356 puntos, luego de que el Gobierno anunció el martes que la economía se expandió un 0,5% anual en el tercer trimestre, muy por debajo de lo esperado por el mercado; en tanto que arrojó una contracción de 0,8% en comparación con el segundo trimestre.

* El peso mayorista argentino ARS=RASL descendió un 0,45% a 1.559,5 por dólar, mientras que el índice accionario MSCI Merval .MMXMRVLGA de la bolsa de Buenos Aires ganaba un 0,43% antes del cierre.

* El sol peruano PEN=PDSB se depreció un 0,53% a 3,4320/3,4330 unidades por dólar, mientras que el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú realizó un swap cambiario por 700 millones de soles. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPE retrocedió un 2,94% a 1.353 puntos.

• Las bolsas latinoamericanas tocan su mínimo desde el pasado diciembre
  • El presidente de México califica de «muy buena» su reunión con EEUU
  • El real brasileño toca mínimos de abril de 2025 frente al dólar
  • El peso chileno cae brevemente a su mínimo de los últimos 22 meses

Actualización con los niveles de cotización de la tarde

Por Tharuniyaa Lakshmi y Shashwat Chauhan

18 nov (Reuters) - La mayoría de las divisas latinoamericanas se depreciaron el miércoles frente a un dólar más fuerte, ya que los operadores siguieron apostando por futuras subidas de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal, mientras que la caída de los precios de las materias primas agravó el panorama.

El dólar se fortaleció a nivel mundial después de que el gobernador de la Fed, Christopher Waller (link), afirmara que el banco central debería ser más agresivo en su respuesta a la inflación y, o bien aprobar una subida de tasas de medio punto en diciembre, o bien dar señales de un ritmo más rápido de subidas en 2027.

La fortaleza global del dólar provocó pérdidas generalizadas en las monedas latinoamericanas.

El peso mexicano MXN= se depreció alrededor de un 2,49 % y se encaminaba a registrar su mayor caída en un solo día desde abril de 2025, tras haber subido durante las últimas tres sesiones.

Por su parte, la presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum (link) afirmó que había mantenido una «reunión muy positiva» con su homólogo estadounidense, Donald Trump, en un momento en que ambos países prosiguen las negociaciones para aliviar las tensiones comerciales.

El real brasileño BRL= cerraba con una caída del 1,63 %, cotizando en torno a su nivel más bajo desde abril de 2025. El Banco Central del país (link) vendió 1 000 millones de dólares en subastas al contado, con el acuerdo de recomprarlos más adelante.

Los inversionistas también esperaban los resultados de la votación sobre las enmiendas al proyecto de ley fiscal del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en el Senado brasileño, prevista para más tarde ese mismo día.

Los activos latinoamericanos se vieron sometidos a una mayor presión debido al descenso de los precios de materias primas como el oro y el cobre, dada la naturaleza orientada a la exportación de algunas de las mayores economías de la región.

El peso chileno CLP=, país productor de cobre, cayó un 1,61 %, hasta su nivel más bajo desde enero de 2025.

La economía chilena se contrajo un 1,8 % en el tercer trimestre (link) respecto al trimestre anterior, según datos del banco central publicados el miércoles, por debajo de las estimaciones del mercado y registrando su mayor caída en seis años.

«Creemos que estos datos del PIB, junto con la moderada cifra de inflación de octubre y la reciente caída de los precios del petróleo, hacen que la balanza se incline hacia un mantenimiento de las tasas en el 4,50 % el próximo mes», afirmó William Jackson, economista jefe para mercados emergentes de Capital Economics.

El índice general de divisas de MSCI .MILA00000CUS cayó un 1,35 % hasta alcanzar su mínimo en diez meses, mientras que el índice de referencia que sigue la evolución de las acciones regionales .MILA00000PUS bajó un 2,97 %, situándose en su nivel más bajo desde diciembre de 2025.

El índice Bovespa de Brasil .BVSP cedió un 1,35 % tras las pérdidas registradas por las empresas relacionadas con las materias primas Vale VALE3.SA y Petrobras PETR4.SA. El índice de referencia mexicano .MXX cerró a la baja por cuarto día consecutivo tras alcanzar máximos históricos la semana pasada.

La empresa chilena SQM SQM-A.SN cayó un 6 % después de que el segundo mayor productor mundial de litio publicara (link) sus resultados del tercer trimestre.

Las acciones latinoamericanas suelen considerarse un refugio frente a la volatilidad relacionada con la IA debido a su escasa exposición a los valores tecnológicos, pero el miércoles se vieron sometidas a presión debido a su gran exposición al mercado de materias primas.

El sector de la IA volvió a ser el centro de atención después de que el gigante de los chips Nvidia NVDA.O pronosticara el martes por la noche unos ingresos trimestrales (link) superiores a las estimaciones de Wall Street.

Panamá también acaparó la atención después de que Moody’s Ratings revisara (link) la perspectiva de su calificación crediticia soberana «Baa3» de «negativa» a «estable», poniendo fin a un período de espera de dos años durante el cual mantuvo una perspectiva «negativa». No obstante, la calificación sigue situándose en el último peldaño de la categoría de «grado de inversión».

El bono en dólares del país con vencimiento en 2032 US698299BN37=TE cotizaba al alza 0,2 céntimos por dólar, según datos de Tradeweb.

• LatAm stocks hit lowest since last December
  • Mexico's President says "very good meeting" with US
  • Brazil's real hits April 2025 lows vs dollar
  • Chile's peso briefly falls to a 22-month low

Updates with afternoon trading levels

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Most Latin American currencies slipped against a firmer dollar on Wednesday as traders continued to bet on future Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, while weaker commodity prices added to the gloom.

The dollar firmed globally after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should be more aggressive in its response to inflation and either approve a half-point rate hike in December or signal a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

The dollar's global strength led to widespread losses in Latin American currencies.

Mexico's peso MXN= depreciated around 2.49%, and was on track to mark its steepest one-day drop since April 2025, after rising for the last three sessions.

Meanwhile, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she had a "very good meeting" with her US counterpart Donald Trump as the two countries pursue negotiations to ease trade tensions.

Brazil's real BRL= was last down 1.63%, trading around its lowest level since April 2025. The country's central bank sold $1 billion in spot dollar auctions with an agreement to repurchase them later.

Investors were also awaiting the results of a vote on President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's fiscal bill amendments in the Brazilian Senate later in the day.

Latin American assets were under further pressure due to receding prices of commodities like gold and copper, given the export-oriented nature of some of the biggest economies in the region.

Copper producer Chile's peso CLP= slipped 1.61%, to its weakest level since January 2025.

Chile's economy contracted 1.8% in the third quarter from the previous three-month period, central bank data showed on Wednesday, undershooting market estimates and marking its biggest decline in six years.

"Our sense is that this GDP release, alongside the soft October inflation print and the recent fall in oil prices, keeps the balance tilted towards a rate hold at 4.50% next month," said William Jackson, chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.

MSCI's broad currency gauge .MILA00000CUS fell 1.35% to a 10-month low, while the benchmark tracking regional stocks .MILA00000PUS dropped 2.97% to its lowest level since December 2025.

Brazil's Bovespa .BVSP eased 1.35% following losses in commodities-related firms Vale VALE3.SA and Petrobras PETR4.SA. The Mexican benchmark .MXX was down for the fourth straight day after hitting record highs last week.

Chilean company SQM SQM-A.SN dropped 6% after the world's second-largest lithium producer reported third-quarter results.

Latin American equities are commonly seen as a refuge from AI-related volatility because of their light exposure to technology stocks, but were under pressure on Wednesday due to their large exposure to the commodities market.

The AI trade was back in focus after chip giant Nvidia NVDA.O forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates late on Tuesday.

Panama was also in focus after Moody's Ratings revised the outlook on its "Baa3" sovereign credit rating to "stable" from "negative", ending an effective two-year wait-and-see period during which it retained a "negative" outlook. The rating, however, remains on the last rung of the "investment grade" category.

The country's 2032 maturity dollar bond US698299BN37=TE was last up 0.2 cents on the dollar, according to Tradeweb data.

The gross domestic product (GDP) of Chile contracted by 1.1% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period the previous year, weighed down by the mining sector, the Central Bank of Chile reported on Wednesday.

"Economic activity decreased by 1.1% on an annual basis. This result was explained by lower investment, a setback that was partly offset by an increase in household and government consumption. From the production perspective, the drop was driven by mining," stated the issuer in the world's leading copper-producing country.

In contrast, the non-mining GDP increased, with notable performance in the agricultural-forestry and trade sectors.

Mining fell by 14.7% in the third quarter of the year, with the decline in copper extraction being the most significant factor affecting this result, according to the institution's report.

"Copper activity was impacted by lower ore grades, maintenance issues, and adverse weather conditions that reduced production from the country's main deposits," the bank noted.

Household consumption, on the other hand, rose by 0.7% during the period, with "increased spending on food and clothing, which was partially offset by lower fuel purchases," according to the National Accounts report.

In its report, the Central Bank revised the GDP growth rate for the first quarter downwards by a tenth, from -0.3% to -0.4%, and for the second quarter revised it upwards by two tenths, from -0.2% to 0.0%.

Chile's Minister of Finance, Jorge Quiroz, acknowledged for the first time last week that the South American country's economy is experiencing a "technical recession."

These results for the third quarter occur in a context marked by historic unemployment figures, with over one million people unemployed across the country, and persistent inflation due to sustained increases in fuel prices.

The agency lowered its growth expectations for this year in September, forecasting that Chile's GDP will expand between 0.25% and 0.75% this year.

Chile's GDP grew by 2.5% in 2025, and inflation ended at 3.5%, its lowest level in five years.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. The acquisition of Cross Border Xpress is expected to enhance these non-aeronautical revenue opportunities, with potential expansions in food and beverage services and VIP lounges anticipated.

Jun 09, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 08, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces the publication of its2025 Sustainability Report, which presents the Companys performance, progress, and key initiatives related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters during 2025.

The report covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025, and was prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards and the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) framework. In addition, it incorporates considerations aligned with other international reporting frameworks, including IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2, issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB).

The full report is available on GAPs website at www.aeropuertosgap.com.mx under the Investors section.

Company Description

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) operates 12 airports throughout Mexicos Pacific region, including the major cities of Guadalajara and Tijuana, the four tourist destinations of Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos, La Paz and Manzanillo, and six other mid-sized cities: Hermosillo, Guanajuato, Morelia, Aguascalientes, Mexicali, and Los Mochis. In February 2006, GAPs shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PAC and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GAP. In April 2015, GAP acquired 100% of Desarrollo de Concessioner Aeroportuarias, S.L., which owns a majority stake in MBJ Airports Limited, a company operating Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay, Jamaica. In accordance with Section 806 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and Article 42 of the Ley del Mercado de Valores, GAP has implemented a whistleblower program, which allows complainants to anonymously and confidentially report suspected activities that involve criminal conduct or violations.

During May 2026, the 12 Mexican airports operated by GAP recorded a 2.8% decrease in total passenger traffic compared to May 2025. Guadalajara airport reported an increase of 7.1%, while Puerto Vallarta, Tijuana and Los Cabos reported a decrease of 14.4%, 9.8%, and 6.0%, respectively, compared to May 2025. With respect to GAPs airports in Jamaica, Montego Bay recorded a decrease of 19.1%, while Montego Bay recorded a decrease of 5.2%.

Jun 01, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Completes Full Acquisition of Cross Border Xpress

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) has successfully finalized its acquisition of Cross Border Xpress, marking a significant milestone in its expansion strategy. The completion of this transaction was officially recorded on 3rd June 2026, following the notarization of a merger agreement that was initially signed on 30th April 2026.

The acquisition involved GAP purchasing the remaining 25 percent stake in Cross Border Xpress, thereby securing full ownership of the facility. This strategic move not only grants GAP complete control over future earnings but also enhances its operational capabilities in the region. Cross Border Xpress operates a unique pedestrian bridge linking a terminal in San Diego, California, directly to Tijuana International Airport, offering a seamless transit experience for ticketed passengers.

By bypassing traditional border crossing queues, the high-traffic facility generates significant revenue, further complementing Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico's existing airport operations in Tijuana. As a leading airport operator, GAP manages 12 airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving multiple cities and popular tourist destinations. This acquisition aligns with GAP's strategy to bolster its position in the aviation sector.

In addition to its core aeronautical services, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico diversifies its revenue streams through non-aeronautical activities, which include commercial services such as car parking, shops, hotels, and restaurants. The acquisition of Cross Border Xpress is expected to enhance these non-aeronautical revenue opportunities, with potential expansions in food and beverage services and VIP lounges anticipated.

Overall, the full acquisition of Cross Border Xpress represents a significant growth opportunity for Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, allowing the company to maximize its operational synergies and enhance its service offerings in the highly competitive airport management sector.

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 20th largest Health care company by market capitalization.
