SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 20th largest Health care company by market capitalization.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Sep 09, 2026: Vesta Repays US$105 Million of Private Debt Ahead of Maturity

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta" or the "Company") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, today announced that it has repaid in full US$105 million of outstanding principal under two private financings, retiring both obligations ahead of their scheduled maturities.

The repayments consisted of US$60 million of 5.31% Series B senior notes due September 22, 2027, issued under the US$125 million note purchase agreement dated September 22, 2017; and US$45 million of 5.85% Tranche B loans due May 31, 2028, outstanding under the US$90 million term loan agreement dated May 31, 2018.

"Retiring these financings ahead of maturity reflects our disciplined approach to balance sheet management and capital allocation," said Juan Sottil, Chief Financial Officer of Vesta. "The transaction simplifies our capital structure, eliminates the related covenants and reporting requirements and provides greater financial flexibility as we continue to execute our Route 2030 strategy. It is also consistent with the financial discipline recognized by S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings in their recent upgrades of Vesta to 'BBB'."

In connection with the repayments, Vesta paid accrued and unpaid interest and the applicable make-whole amounts under each agreement. All amounts outstanding under both agreements have been repaid in full, and the agreements have been terminated.

May 26, 2026: Vesta Announces Two New Lease Agreements Totaling More Than 570 Thousand Square Feet in Monterrey

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta" or the "Company") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully-integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, announced that it has entered into two new lease agreements for a total of more than 570 thousand square feet in Monterrey, reflecting the continued progress on the Company's Route 2030 strategic growth plan.

At Vesta Park Apodaca, one of the industrial parks with the best connectivity and building quality in Monterrey, Vesta leased two buildings to European companies specializing in industrial manufacturing and the production of industrial equipment linked to critical infrastructure and specialized supply chains.

These operations will strengthen the region's industrial ecosystem and contribute to the growth of strategic sectors in North America, particularly those related to the expansion of data center infrastructure.

"We are very pleased with the demand for space we are seeing related to the data center sector in North America. At Vesta, we will continue to serve the fastest-growing industries," said Mario Chacon, Vesta's Chief Commercial Officer.

With these transactions, Vesta continues to consolidate its position as one of the leading developers of industrial infrastructure in Mexico, driving projects aligned with the trends of digitalization, nearshoring and expansion of industrial capabilities in the region.

Sep 09, 2026: Vesta Repays US$105 Million of Private Debt Ahead of Maturity

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta" or the "Company") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, today announced that it has repaid in full US$105 million of outstanding principal under two private financings, retiring both obligations ahead of their scheduled maturities.

The repayments consisted of US$60 million of 5.31% Series B senior notes due September 22, 2027, issued under the US$125 million note purchase agreement dated September 22, 2017; and US$45 million of 5.85% Tranche B loans due May 31, 2028, outstanding under the US$90 million term loan agreement dated May 31, 2018.

"Retiring these financings ahead of maturity reflects our disciplined approach to balance sheet management and capital allocation," said Juan Sottil, Chief Financial Officer of Vesta. "The transaction simplifies our capital structure, eliminates the related covenants and reporting requirements and provides greater financial flexibility as we continue to execute our Route 2030 strategy. It is also consistent with the financial discipline recognized by S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings in their recent upgrades of Vesta to 'BBB'."

In connection with the repayments, Vesta paid accrued and unpaid interest and the applicable make-whole amounts under each agreement. All amounts outstanding under both agreements have been repaid in full, and the agreements have been terminated.

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta" or the "Company") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully-integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, announced that it has entered into two new lease agreements for a total of more than 570 thousand square feet in Monterrey, reflecting the continued progress on the Company's Route 2030 strategic growth plan.

At Vesta Park Apodaca, one of the industrial parks with the best connectivity and building quality in Monterrey, Vesta leased two buildings to European companies specializing in industrial manufacturing and the production of industrial equipment linked to critical infrastructure and specialized supply chains.

These operations will strengthen the region's industrial ecosystem and contribute to the growth of strategic sectors in North America, particularly those related to the expansion of data center infrastructure.

"We are very pleased with the demand for space we are seeing related to the data center sector in North America. At Vesta, we will continue to serve the fastest-growing industries," said Mario Chacon, Vesta's Chief Commercial Officer.

With these transactions, Vesta continues to consolidate its position as one of the leading developers of industrial infrastructure in Mexico, driving projects aligned with the trends of digitalization, nearshoring and expansion of industrial capabilities in the region.

Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de scores a Z = 0.73 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.1 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Asset Quality Index

Sales Growth Index

Depreciation Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de has a Beneish M-Score of -4.88 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]. An M-score of less than -1.78 is considered normal. However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 16 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.36; a deterioration from 0.35 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Altman-Z score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores a Z = 1.23 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.24 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Asset Quality Index

Sales Growth Index

Depreciation Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has a Beneish M-Score of -4.77 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]. An M-score of less than -1.78 is considered normal. However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 16 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

Piotroski F-Score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 5 for the half year-ended 30 June 2025 indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores an O = -9.845

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

Beneish M-score of Kimberly-Clark de Mexico,B de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

ADRS AND DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.35; a deterioration from 0.32 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.34 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

However Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de debt to equity ratio of 0.35 compares unfavorably with the Real estate sector median of 0.14.

Debt to Assets Ratio of Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.22; a deterioration from 0.21 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and an improvement from 0.23 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Altman-Z score of Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de scores a Z = 1.27 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; an improvement from 1.12 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a deterioration from 1.69 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Piotroski F-Score of Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de

Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de has achieved a high Piotroski F-Score of 7 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating solid financial health and operational efficiency. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. A strong score suggests that Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de is not only generating solid earnings and cash flow but also managing its balance sheet prudently positioning it well for sustained growth and investor confidence.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta,B. de scores an O = -8.4124

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

The Mexican Open-Pit segment remains the largest contributor, generating $2,511.9 million in the second quarter of 2026, or 57.6% of the segment total. Its 43.1% year-over-year increase outpaced the consolidated growth rate, reflecting higher metal prices and a 2.2% increase in copper sales volumes. The IMMSA unit posted the strongest percentage growth at 49.5%, with net sales rising from $179.3 million to $267.9 million, driven by higher zinc and silver prices and a 0.4% increase in zinc sales volumes. The Peruvian operations grew 34.5%, the slowest of the three segments, as copper sales volumes declined 6.5% due to lower ore grades and mineral milled at Toquepala and Cuajone. On a six-month basis, IMMSA's growth was even more pronounced at 75.2%, while Mexican Open-Pit rose 41.4% and Peruvian operations increased 29.5%. Operating income tells a similar story: IMMSA's operating income surged 395.0% to $88.0 million in Q2 2026, while Mexican Open-Pit operating income rose 62.9% to $1,610.7 million and Peruvian operating income increased 60.5% to $935.9 million. The Mexican Open-Pit segment contributed 61.4% of total operating income, underscoring its central role in the Company's profitability.

By Liz Hampton and Arathy Somasekhar

DENVER, Nov 18 (Reuters) - US crude stocks, gasoline and distillate inventories rose last week, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday.

Crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 58,000-barrel rise.

Crude stocks at the Cushing, Oklahoma, delivery hub USOICC=ECI fell by 1.2 million barrels in the week, the EIA said.

Oil futures extended losses following the report. Global Brent crude futures LCOc1 were trading at $91.85 a barrel, down $1.29, at 10:38 a.m. ET (1538 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate futures CLc1 were down $1.81 to $84.2 a barrel.

Refinery crude runs USOICR=ECI fell by 129,000 barrels per day in the week, the EIA said, while utilization rates USOIRU=ECI rose by 0.5 percentage points in the week to 95.7%.

US gasoline stocks USOILG=ECI rose by 5.2 million barrels in the week to 215.9 million barrels, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 1.6 million-barrel build.

Distillate stockpiles USOILD=ECI, which include diesel and heating oil, rose by 1.6 million barrels in the week to 104.9 million barrels, versus expectations for a 1.3 million-barrel rise, the EIA data showed.

Net US crude imports USOICI=ECI fell by 2.15 million barrels per day, EIA said, while exports rose by 1.03 million bpd to 4.49 million bpd.

(Reporting by Liz Hampton in Denver and Arathy Somasekhar in Houston;)

(( liz.hampton@thomsonreuters.com ))

Adds further comments, context

By Marcela Ayres

BRASILIA, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan signaled on Wednesday that the government would move ahead with additional fiscal measures in the near term, arguing that improving public finances is essential to create room for lower interest rates.

Speaking at an event hosted by Bradesco BBI after a meeting with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva earlier in the day, Durigan said the fiscal package currently in the Senate is only a "first step" and should not be viewed as the government's fiscal roadmap for the coming years.

"We are going to adopt new and additional measures right away," Durigan said.

Since Lula's surprise reelection last month sparked a sharp depreciation of Brazilian assets, investors have been eagerly awaiting structural fiscal measures and clearer signals from Lula on his upcoming economic team and agenda for the next term.

Durigan described fiscal policy as the government's main tool to address economic challenges, saying Brazil needed to strengthen its fiscal position to help create the conditions for the central bank to cut borrowing costs.

He also said the government should address exemptions and carve-outs from the fiscal target framework in order to reach the midpoint of its goal, adding there are no plans to control free capital flow in Brazil, nor to change the inflation target.

On the economy, he said growth is expected to slow next year but added that he does not foresee a recession.

The minister also said the government would seek to improve existing public programs rather than expand them, with the aim of restoring "rationality" to spending.

The administration does not expect additional revenue from the country's consumer tax reform, Durigan added.

(Reporting by Marcela Ayres; Editing by Fernando Cardoso)

(( marcela.ayres@thomsonreuters.com ; +55 11 5047-2444; ))

PORTUGUESE END-OF-DAY STOCK REPORT

The European Commission projects EU real GDP growth of 1.4% in 2026 and 2027, rising to 1.5% in 2028, while the euro area is seen expanding 1.2% in 2026-27 and 1.3% in 2028. Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said Portugal's growth would stay above the EU average, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and EU funds, notably the Recovery and Resilience Plan in 2026.

For EDP Distribuicao, the tie between economic activity and electricity consumption is central: the company operates most of Portugal's medium- and high-voltage grid and serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers nationwide. A pickup in domestic demand could lift volumes, while grid modernization and renewable integration projects, partly financed through EU funds, may boost efficiency and reliability.

However, upside is not guaranteed. Demand depends on energy efficiency gains, weather, and regulatory decisions, and the Commission's baseline cites downside risks such as geopolitical tensions and the lagged impact of monetary policy on spending, which could temper gains even if Portugal outperforms.

Por Utkarsh Hathi y Ragini Mathur

18 nov (Reuters) - El Nasdaq, que tiene una gran presencia de empresas tecnológicas, cotizaba casi estable el miércoles en una jornada volátil, mientras los inversores esperaban el precio de la salida a bolsa de Anthropic, que se considera que será el próximo catalizador del sector de la inteligencia artificial, después de que las optimistas previsiones de ingresos de Nvidia disiparon en parte las preocupaciones de los inversores.

Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O bajaban un 0,3%, a pesar de que la empresa anunció el martes que espera unos ingresos en el cuarto trimestre de 130.000 millones de dólares, con un margen de error del 3%. Según datos recopilados por LSEG, los analistas habían estimado en promedio ventas de 125.250 millones de dólares.

La incertidumbre en torno a las perspectivas de Nvidia tras la repentina salida del ex presidente ejecutivo Jensen Huang la semana pasada había sacudido la confianza de los inversores en el sector de la IA. El martes, el directorio de la empresa descartó la idea de volver a contratar a Huang, pese a una campaña para que regrese.

"La cuestión central a la que se enfrenta Nvidia no está relacionada con este último informe de resultados (…) sino que tiene más que ver con cómo podría ser la empresa dentro de tres a cinco años sin un líder visionario como Jensen y a medida que se intensifica la competencia de otros fabricantes de chips", dijo Jay Peters, gestor de carteras de NewEdge Wealth.

Otras acciones del sector de los chips cotizaban estables o bajaban. Intel INTC.O caía un 2,1%, mientras que Advanced Micro Devices AMD.O y Micron MU.O bajaban alrededor de un 1%.

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

EL S&P 500 Y EL NASDAQ SE ESTABILIZAN MIENTRAS NVIDIA SE MANTENGA A FLOTE

Las acciones estadounidenses presentan un panorama mixto en las primeras horas de la sesión bursátil de este miércoles: el Nasdaq Composite .IXIC avanza, mientras que el S&P 500 .SPX y el Dow .DJI retroceden.

S&P 500, NASDAQ FIND FOOTING AS NVIDIA TREADS WATER

US stocks are a mixed bag in the early stages of trading on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC advancing, while the S&P 500 .SPX and Dow .DJI retreat.

Nvidia NVDA.O shares are down nearly 1%, giving up their premarket gains, after the chipmaker and epicenter of the AI trade reported quarterly results after the closing bell on Tuesday, while board Chairman Harvey Jones opened a conference call with investors by saying co-founder Jensen Huang would not be rehired as CEO.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's late October meeting, when the central bank held rates steady, are due later in the day.

Markets have been completely pricing in a rate hike from the Fed at its December meeting, in part due to economic data that shows an economy on solid footing while price pressures remain, and comments from central bank officials indicating more hikes are needed.

US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller again floated the idea of an outsized 50-basis-point hike on Wednesday, saying the central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation that he fears is changing public psychology about prices, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

Among the major S&P sectors, consumer discretionary .SPLRCD is leading gains, buoyed in part by a jump in TJX TJX.N after the off-price retailer forecast upbeat annual sales, while energy shares .SPNY are under pressure.

ANNA NORDSTROM, HEAD OF THE MARKETS GROUP, FEDERAL RESERVE BANK OF NEW YORK, PREPARED REMARKS AT THE 2026 FX MARKET STRUCTURE CONFERENCE, NEW YORK CITY, AS RELEASED BY THE NEW YORK FEDERAL RESERVE

ANNA NORDSTROM, HEAD OF THE MARKETS GROUP, FEDERAL RESERVE BANK OF NEW YORK, PREPARED REMARKS AT THE 2026 FX MARKET STRUCTURE CONFERENCE, NEW YORK CITY, AS RELEASED BY THE NEW YORK FEDERAL RESERVE

NOVEMBER 16, 2026

SPEAKERS: ANNA NORDSTROM, HEAD OF THE MARKETS GROUP, FEDERAL RESERVE BANK OF NEW YORK

[*] NORDSTROM: Good morning. I'm pleased to see so many of you here in person and virtually, for our third annual FX Market Structure Conference. This event brings together many distinguished experts from global financial markets. Today's agenda is intended to encourage dialogue around important themes in the foreign exchange (FX) market landscape. I am very much looking forward to our discussions.

Before I begin, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to our organizing committee and to the many contributors across the New York Fed who have helped with this event. Let me also offer the usual disclaimer: The views I express this morning are my own and do not necessarily reflect those of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York or others in the Federal Reserve System.

Setting the Stage

The foreign exchange market is critical to our global economy. It serves as the backbone of the global financial system, facilitating the flow of funds in support of international trade, payments, and investment. As such, it is necessary to understand the market structure and the rapid changes underway.

In my remarks, I'll start by briefly discussing the New York Fed's role in the FX market. I'll then set the stage for our panel discussions by sharing two observations on the market that stood out to me over the past year. The first relates to the relative resiliency of the FX market, despite heightened volatility in many other markets. The second is the accelerated pace of technological change. To conclude, I will say a few words about the FX Global Code, as we approach its next strategic review. I hope these observations encourage more discussion and reflection on the future structure of the market.

The New York Fed's Role in the FX Market

So, what role does the New York Fed play in the foreign exchange market, and why do we closely monitor its development? First, we are a regular participant in the market. We conduct FX transactions on behalf of customers such as the U.S. government and, when requested occasionally, on behalf of official sector account holders. Second, as fiscal agent of the United States Treasury, we conduct FX intervention operations for the Treasury's Exchange Stabilization Fund (ESF) and on behalf of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) for the System Open Market Account (SOMA), when directed to do so by policymakers. Finally, we manage the central bank liquidity swap lines of the Federal Reserve System, which are aimed at supporting global dollar funding markets.

Given these mandates, it is important that we have a deep understanding of the structure and function of the market to most effectively carry out our responsibilities on behalf of policymakers. This is one reason why the New York Fed also sponsors the Foreign Exchange Committee (FXC) and participates in the Global Foreign Exchange Committee (GFXC). These committees convene the public and private sectors to discuss and maintain best practices in the FX market, including through the FX Global Code, which I will return to later.

FX Market Resilience

Turning to my first observation, the FX market has remained resilient in the face of great uncertainty in the global economy and financial markets over the past year. The onset of the conflict in the Middle East triggered sharp increases in energy prices. This prompted a repricing of the expected path of monetary policy globally, and it affected broader risk sentiment, leading to heightened volatility across a number of markets.

However, market participants broadly characterized the spillovers to foreign exchange markets as limited, and measures of FX volatility remained relatively contained. This was particularly true relative to energy and rates markets. Market functioning metrics also suggested robust trading and liquidity conditions. Bid-ask spreads were generally stable, market depth and price impact measures were resilient, and settlement and post-trade processes functioned smoothly.

Signs of resilience were also seen in emerging market (EM) currencies, including a sustained interest in carry trade activity. Market participants commented that this reflected more solid economic fundamentals as well as structural improvements, including deeper local capital markets, a robust domestic institutional investor base, and improved market infrastructure, such as electronification and extended local trading hours.

In this context, I am eager to hear our panelists discuss the themes impacting the foreign exchange market and EM market structure, and to hear perspectives on the factors contributing to the relatively contained volatility environment in FX.

Accelerating Technological Advancement

Another important development I want to highlight is the accelerated pace and rapid adoption of new technologies.

Artificial intelligence (AI) usage in the FX market is moving quickly from testing into real-world use, in areas such as workflow automation, pre-trade analytics, and transaction cost analysis. Market participants often point to AI's ability to quickly and efficiently absorb large amounts of data and information, which can improve execution outcomes and broaden the range of participants with access to sophisticated tools. Of course, there is also a discussion about potential existing or emerging risks as technological change accelerates. This includes the potential for less-transparent trading activity and an increasingly correlated behavior from use of similar models. As such, it is critical that risk and governance models keep up with the accelerated pace of market activity.

In addition, settlement technologies are changing. Introductions of blockchain and forms of tokenized money can support faster cross-border movements of funds. This has the potential to accelerate transaction and settlement lifecycles, reduce operational costs, and extend trading and settlement hours toward 24/7 activity. And of course, it could facilitate near-instant or atomic settlement of FX transactions, which, in turn, could support the broader market trend of shortened settlement cycles for securities transactions. Still, questions remain as to whether such changes could result in thinner FX market liquidity, reduced netting efficiencies, and greater volatility during less active periods.

While it is unclear how this will play out, these forces will certainly continue to shape the future structure of the market, and it is important we understand the trade-offs between the benefits and risks. We gain insights on this through many channels, including through our FXC and GFXC discussions, as well as through bilateral discussions and events like today's conference. I look forward to hearing the perspectives of our panelists today, including what we may already be seeing in these areas in emerging markets.

The FX Global Code

That brings me, finally, to the FX Global Code. We are approaching the 10th anniversary of the Code, and heading into next year the GFXC will kick off a three-year strategic review. The regular reviews play an important role in ensuring that the Code remains fit for purpose, and that it keeps pace with a changing marketplace and new technological developments over time. In a decentralized global market where there is no single exchange or regulator, these principles help build trust and transparency among a wide range of market participants.

As part of the review process, the GFXC seeks extensive input from a diverse set of market participants. The process includes a market participant survey, feedback from local foreign exchange committees in over 20 jurisdictions and input from the Bank for International Settlement (BIS) Markets Committee, which represents 27 central banks globally. All of these channels play an important role in helping to frame the scope of the Code review.

The Code itself plays a critical role in setting out global principles that promote the integrity and effective functioning of the wholesale FX market. It was developed via a partnership between central banks and the private sector and is maintained through the GFXC. I was fortunate to have been involved in the original launch of the Code, alongside many of my colleagues here at the New York Fed. It has been great to see the benefits of broader adoption across such a diverse market, and I look forward to hearing the GFXC's leadership discuss it in the conference today.

Closing

Let me close where I began. We are here today because the FX market is vitally important, and the function of the market impacts corporations, households, financial markets, and the strength and resilience of the global economy. The structure of this market must rest on a strong foundation that can be both durable enough to provide stability, but also flexible enough to evolve. We all see that the market structure is changing quickly, though each of us may be experiencing this in different ways. I hope that today's conference can bring together these perspectives to build a richer understanding of what may lie ahead.

I look forward to the discussions today.

END

• Indexes: Dow falls 0.75%, S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq up 0.5%
  • TJX jumps after forecasting upbeat annual sales
  • Investors await Anthropic IPO pricing
  • Waller says Fed needs to get more aggressive in inflation response

Updates after market opens

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nov 18 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq rose on Wednesday in choppy trading as investors awaited Anthropic's IPO pricing for the next catalyst in the AI trade after Nvidia's upbeat revenue forecast eased some investor concerns about the chip bellwether's future.

Nvidia NVDA.O shares were down 0.3% even after the company said on Tuesday it expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. Analysts on average had estimated $125.25 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Uncertainty around Nvidia's outlook following former CEO Jensen Huang's sudden exit last week had rattled investor confidence in the AI trade. On Tuesday, the company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang amid a campaign to bring him back.

"The central question Nvidia faces is not related to this latest earnings report... as it’s more about what the company may look like in 3-5 years without a visionary leader like Jensen and as competition from other chipmakers takes shape," said Jay Peters, portfolio manager at NewEdge Wealth.

Other chip stocks were flat to lower. Intel INTC.O was down 2.1%, while Advanced Micro Devices AMD.Oand Micron MU.Oedged about 1% lower.

Neocloud stocks shed their premarket gains, with CoreWeave CRWV.O and Nebius NBIS.O falling 5.7% and 2%, respectively.

Peters said Nvidia was in a "show me" camp, with investors likely to scrutinize every development at the company, which could keep the stock range-bound for some time.

With Nvidia's results out of the way, attention is shifting to the pricing of Anthropic's ANT.O initial public offering later in the day, a key test of Wall Street's appetite for companies tied to the AI boom.

The Claude chatbot creator is eyeing a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion in what would be the first-ever IPO by a frontier AI model developer.

At 10:04 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI fell 383.05 points, or 0.75%, to 50,380.71, the S&P 500 .SPX gained 0.12 points, or 0.00%, to 7,340.65 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC gained 130.42 points, or 0.54%, to 24,458.80.

Six of 11 sectors on the benchmark S&P 500 traded in the red, while the heavyweight technology group .SPLRCT gained 0.4%.

Financial .SPSY and healthcare SPXHC stocks led the losses, falling 0.8% each.

On the flip side, the consumer discretionary sector .SPLRCD gained 1%.

Off-price retailer TJX TJX.N jumped 8.6% after forecasting upbeat annual sales, banking on strong demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Target TGT.N shares gained 5% after it reported a third straight quarter of better-than-expected results as its recovery takes root.

FED IN FOCUS

The Federal Reserve's Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to either raise the interest rate by half a point at its December meeting or signal a more aggressive response to inflation in its communication.

Investors will scan the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for clues on the central bank's policy path.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Among other movers, Take-Two Interactive TTWO.O shares gained 6.9% as the global rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game was set to begin on Wednesday across markets.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.1-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, while advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.43-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 2 new 52-week highs and 7 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 11 new highs and 209 new lows.

(Reporting by Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Sriraj Kalluvila and Maju Samuel)

(( utkarshtushar.hathi@thomsonreuters.com ))

At 10:04 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI fell 383.05 points, or 0.75%, to 50,380.71, the S&P 500 .SPX gained 0.12 points, or 0.00%, to 7,340.65 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC gained 130.42 points, or 0.54%, to 24,458.80.

Six of 11 sectors on the benchmark S&P 500 traded in the red, while the heavyweight technology group .SPLRCT gained 0.4%.

Financial .SPSY and healthcare SPXHC stocks led the losses, falling 0.8% each.

On the flip side, the consumer discretionary sector .SPLRCD gained 1%.

Off-price retailer TJX TJX.N jumped 8.6% after forecasting upbeat annual sales, banking on strong demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Target TGT.N shares gained 5% after it reported a third straight quarter of better-than-expected results as its recovery takes root.

FED IN FOCUS

The Federal Reserve's Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to either raise the interest rate by half a point at its December meeting or signal a more aggressive response to inflation in its communication.

Investors will scan the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for clues on the central bank's policy path.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Among other movers, Take-Two Interactive TTWO.O shares gained 6.9% as the global rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game was set to begin on Wednesday across markets.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.1-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, while advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.43-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 2 new 52-week highs and 7 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 11 new highs and 209 new lows.

New Orleans Branch Announces Appointment to Board of Directors

For immediate release: November 18, 2026

  • Press Release

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta announces the appointment of Douglas S. Downing to the New Orleans Branch board of directors. He was appointed by the Board of Governors to fill an unexpired term ending December 31, 2027.

Downing is the chief financial officer of Canal Barge Company in New Orleans as well as its holding company, Redwood Holdings. He also serves as treasurer of the New Orleans Military & Maritime Academy and is a member of Beta Gamma Sigma, an international business honor society. Downing earned a bachelor of arts from the University of Virginia and a master of business administration from Tulane University's Freeman School of Business.

Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta branch directors provide economic information from their industries and the branch territory to the district Bank's president and head office directors, who use the information in discussing monetary policy options and making discount rate recommendations. The Board of Governors appoints three of the New Orleans Branch directors, and the Atlanta head office directors appoint four.

EUR/USD dropped to a fresh 19-month low on Wednesday as US dollar bulls kept control, driven by hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric. That rhetoric may be misplaced though, and may be a case of shouting into the wind.

US interest rates rallied after last week's October CPI and PPI reports suggested inflation will stay above the Fed's target, prompting FOMC officials to say price growth is a serious problem. The latest comments came from Governor Christopher Waller today. He argued that the Fed should respond more aggressively, either by approving a 50bps hike in December or by signaling a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

The growing hawkishness could prove premature, because energy markets point to slower price growth in future inflation reports. Several energy products are showing bearish price action. Brent futures LCOc1 are consolidating losses from the October monthly high and trading below the 200-DMA. Diesel futures HOc1 have fallen below the 200-DMA and reached a 3-month low. Gasoline futures RBc1 have hit an 8-month low. This broad-based decline suggests upcoming inflation data could show smaller price increases.

If that happens, the Fed may have to walk back its hawkish messaging. The US dollar and US interest rates could then soften significantly, and the large net-long dollar position NETUSDG10= could be reduced.

That unwinding could set off a significant short squeeze in EUR/USD, which would reverse the pair's recent weakness.

For more click on FXBUZ

(Christopher Romano is a Reuters market analyst. The views expressed are his own)

BRASILIA, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan signaled on Wednesday that the government would move ahead with additional fiscal measures in the near term.

Speaking at an event hosted by Bradesco BBI after a meeting with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva earlier in the day, Durigan said the fiscal package currently in the Senate is only a "first step" and should not be viewed as the government's fiscal roadmap for the coming years.

Updates prices at 1500 GMT

By Eric Onstad

LONDON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Copper prices slumped to their weakest in seven months on Wednesday as speculators rushed to sell, spurred by worries over rising inflation and a buoyant dollar.

A slide through key support levels triggered more selling from computer-driven funds that use algorithms and technical signals for trading.

Benchmark three-month copper CMCU3 on the London Metal Exchange fell for a fifth consecutive session, dropping 4.8% to $12,590.50 a metric ton by 1500 GMT, its lowest since April 9.

"It seems like people are throwing in the towel after we took out quite a few technical levels, adding to the momentum selling," said Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank in Copenhagen.

"It's the inflation scare, the risk of higher funding costs that's weighing on risk sentiment. AI was a trigger, but it's not really the driver."

US Comex copper futures HGc3 slid 5.2% to a seven-month low of $5.67 per lb.

A selloff in AI companies recently has fuelled worries about data centre projects, a key growth area for copper demand. But tech and AI stocks steadied on Wednesday, which failed to prop up copper, Hansen said. MKTS/GLOB

The dollar held steady near a 19-month high as US economic data and comments from US Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for increases to interest rates.

A stronger US currency makes dollar-priced metals costlier for buyers using other currencies. USD/

The most traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange SCFv1 fell 3.4% to 97,920 yuan ($14,689.69) a ton.

Speculative selling overwhelmed concerns about localised shortages in top consumer China, where the premium paid to import copper jumped to a record high of $360 a ton on Wednesday.

Other metals were swept into the downdraft, with LME aluminium CMAL3 sliding 2.4% to $2,864 a ton after touching its lowest in almost a year in the previous session.

LME zinc CMZN3 shed 2.9% to $3,567.50 a ton, its weakest since July 29, lead CMPB3 dipped 0.2% to $1,868.50, having sunk to its lowest in more than a month, and nickel CMNI3 gave up 2.9% to $15,985.

Tin CMSN3 dropped by 5.1% to $42,765, its lowest in nearly eight months.

($1 = 6.6659 Chinese yuan renminbi)

(Reporting by Eric Onstad; Additional reporting by Ashitha Shivaprasad in Bengaluru
Editing by David Goodman and Shilpi Majumdar)

(( eric.onstad@thomsonreuters.com ; +44 20 7542 7093; Twitter https://twitter.com/reutersEricO; Reuters Messaging: eric.onstad.thomsonreuters.com@reuters.net /))

The president of Mexico, Claudia Sheinbaum, emphasized on Wednesday a "very good meeting" with U.S. President Donald Trump, despite the recent tariff threats issued by the White House chief concerning the caravans of Central American migrants crossing Mexico with the intention of entering U.S. territory.

"We had a very good meeting with Trump and his team," the Mexican leader stated in a social media message about the encounter with the U.S. leader on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit taking place in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

"We continue to move forward on our common agenda," Sheinbaum noted, highlighting cooperation with Washington despite the threats regarding the potential influx of migrants.

Trump recently warned Mexico that he would double the current tariffs if it does not take action to stop the migrants, referring to an attempt at "invasion" of the United States. Sheinbaum responded shortly thereafter, asserting that authorities in Mexico discourage these individuals seeking to reach the U.S. and that most return to their countries of origin.

The campaign kicked off on Thursday, November 5, at around 12:01 a.m. (central Mexico time) on the online stores of Walmart, Bodega Aurrera, and Sam's Club. In physical stores, it began approximately at 8:00 a.m. (central Mexico time), although the timing varied at some locations depending on their proximity. When does the Irresistible Sale 2026 end? The Irresistible Sale will conclude on Wednesday, November 18, around midnight for online stores and approximately at 10:00 p.m. for physical stores.
